50969552.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to His6-tagged BRD2 expressed in Escherichia coli by surface plasmon resonance assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface Plasmon Resonance. Binding experiments with BRD4-BD12 and BRD2-BD12 were conducted at 25 °C on at least three occasions on a T200 BLAcore instrument. In all cases, a CMS chip with amine coupled protein was used. Flow cells of a CMS chip were first activated with 0.2 M N-ethyl-N’-(diethylaminoethyl)carbodiimide (EDC) and 0.05 M N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS). Typically 0.1–2 mg/mL BRD4-BD12/BRD2-BD12 at pH 4.5–5.5 in NaAc was then injected at 10 μL/min for 1–2 min, resulting in >5KRU of protein immobilized on the surface. The surface was neutralized with ethanolamine and extensively washed in the running buffer 50 mM HEPES pH7.5, 150 mM NaCl. Compounds were titrated as a triplicate dilution starting at 10–20 μM. Sensorgrams and equilibrium binding curves were analyzed with BIAevaluation (GE Healthcare) using a 1:1 binding model. Parameters were derived from an equilibrium binding analysis. The equilibrium Kd was calculating using a 1:1 binding model, response = concentration × Rmax/(Concentration + Kd) + offset.

original_paragraph.Results: SPR Kd Determination. To obtain label-free confirmation of binding to the BET bromodomains and an equilibrium binding constant, exemplars were tested in a surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay. Compound 34 was found to have a Kd of 2–3 μM for BRD2 and BRD4 (Table 4), consistent with the micromolar TR-FRET IC50 values in Table 3.
